literal: Excellence possessing wealthy people's small distress, rain cloud drought having become intense like that it possesses.
translation: When wealthy people of excellent character suffer a brief period of poverty, it is as devastating to the world as a rain cloud failing in a severe drought.
modern: சிறந்த பண்புடைய செல்வர்கள் சிறிது வறுமை அடைவது, மழைமேகம் வறண்டு போவதைப் போன்ற தன்மையை உடையது.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the wealth of the generous with the useless wealth discussed in this chapter. The word 'cīr' refers to the excellence of a generous character, while 'tuṉi' means distress or poverty. When such noble people experience even a brief period of poverty, the world feels the loss deeply. The poet compares this to a rain cloud ('māri') becoming dry ('vaṟam'), showing that just as all life depends on rain, many depend on the generous wealthy.
